transfer_edges.explanation: SQL JOIN logic maps directly to pd.merge(how=...) — your WHERE, GROUP BY, and JOIN intuition transfers
Filtering NULLs and WHERE clauses transfer to pandas boolean indexing and dropna()
PyTorch nn.Module uses class inheritance and __init__/forward pattern you already know
Tensor operations in PyTorch mirror NumPy: reshape, broadcasting, slicing all work the same way
Same gradient descent optimization framework — only the activation and loss function change
Random Forest = ensemble of Decision Trees with bagging — you already understand 70% of it
Distributions are direct applications of probability axioms you already understand
Hypothesis testing is built directly on distributions — p-values come from the CDF you know
Python loop patterns and indexing logic transfer to NumPy vectorized operations
Backpropagation is gradient descent applied to neural networks — you understand the optimization concept
Neural networks are sequences of matrix multiplications — your linear algebra intuition is the foundation
Both are ensemble tree methods — Random Forest experience makes Gradient Boosting 50% easier to grasp
Both are supervised classifiers — understanding decision boundaries from Logistic Regression helps
